extraction: Raw NED ascii_bar main-information rows, values unmodified; only the single data line (the one beginning "1|") is kept from each response and the shared header written once. All 37 queried names resolved: 30 on the first pass, 7 (NGC 4650A, UGC 9796, IC 1689, ARP 230, NGC 4632, NGC 6156, UGC 4385) on a second pass after transient no-response failures. Rows were then DEDUPLICATED on (Object Name, RA, Dec), which collapsed 1 duplicate rows arising from distinct query names that NED cross-identifies to the same object; see cross_identifications.
note: SUPPLEMENTARY. Positions and redshifts for the 40 kinematically confirmed PRGs are already carried by yu2026_table1_confirmed_PRGs.tsv (Yu et al. 2026 took them from NED), and NGC 4632 / NGC 6156 by Deg et al. 2023 Table 1. NED TAP was unusable throughout this acquisition window (every sync query timed out; batched queries returned HTTP 202), so the classic objsearch CGI was used instead. This file adds independent NED positions, heliocentric velocities, redshifts and an apparent magnitude for the systems inventoried in POLAR_RINGS.md, plus the cross-identifications recorded above.

cross_identifications.comment: VERIFIED by two independent single-name queries returning byte-identical rows. This object is PRC A-02 in Yu et al. 2026 Table 1. CONSEQUENCE: the Khoperskov et al. 2014 dark-halo-axis-ratio roster lists "ESO 415-G26" and "MCG-5-7-1" as SEPARATE entries with different references (1987ApJ...314..439W vs 1996ASPC..106..168C + 2013AJ....145...34S), so that roster most likely double-counts one galaxy and contains 20 distinct systems, not 21. Stated as an inference, not a certainty: it is also possible that "MCG-5-7-1" in that figure caption denotes a different object under a mistyped designation.
Arp 230 = IC 51 = PRC B-01. Expected, not a new finding.

These are NOT the same entry: the bare name AM 1934-563 resolves to a galaxy TRIPLE (type GTrpl, 294.66646 -56.45439, z=0.038904) while PGC 089058 resolves to the individual member AM 1934-563 NED02 (294.66002 -56.45796, z=0.038857). PRC B-18 in Yu et al. 2026 is PGC 089058, i.e. the MEMBER. Both rows are retained.

known_quirks: The query "NGC 5907" returns a row whose Object Name is the compound designation "NGC 5907:[IDD2022] X026", but its position (228.97183, +56.32988), magnitude (11.12) and reference count (600) are those of the galaxy NGC 5907 itself, not of a sub-component. Treat the row as NGC 5907 but do not propagate the compound name.
